title: Strategies under a pickoff limit in baseball: A zero-sum sequential game with multilevel models
summary: Recently, Major League Baseball (MLB) limited pitchers to three pickoff attempts, creating a cat-and-mouse game between pitcher and runner. Each failed attempt adds pressure on the pitcher to avoid using another, and the runner can intensify this pressure by extending their leadoff toward the next base. We model this dynamic as a two-player zero-sum sequential game in which the runner first chooses a lead distance, and then the pitcher chooses whether to attempt a pickoff.
